name: popup
description: A modal panel: a title, a body (free text, a single input field, or a gallery + text-icon selector), and a bottom action row of one or two buttons, shown over a real full-viewport dimmed backdrop that a trigger button opens and the bottom row's own buttons (or Escape/backdrop click) close. No close/X control -- dismissal is via the bottom row's own buttons.

props.name: type
props.description: Sets data-type on .ds-popup__body. "text" renders free paragraphs (Penpot's "Summary"); "input" composes a real .ds-input field (Penpot's "Description"); "gallery" composes a real gallery filmstrip plus a gallery-image type="text-icon" selector -- a smaller answer to Penpot's "Image-sliders", see rationale.

props.name: size
props.description: small (500px, Figma's confirmations), medium (800px, Add Description and Summary), or large (1200px, not from a Figma frame yet). Sets data-size on .ds-popup.

props.name: placement
props.description: "center" (default: centered over a full-viewport backdrop dimmed 50%) or "anchored" (a confirmation: 10px under the trigger that opened it, at least 20px from the viewport edge, backdrop dimmed 30% -- see component.js's positionAnchored() and style.css). Sets data-placement on .ds-popup-overlay.

props.name: preview
props.description: inline: render the popup open, in the page flow (backdrop included), without the hidden attribute -- data-preview="inline". Documentation only (the site's Popups card, Figma D_SYSTEM node 103:4815); never in product UI.

rationale:
Styled to Figma's popup-medium (application file, nodes 150:16627, 150:16661, 150:16695, 150:16729), superseding the earlier Penpot values. The panel is bg.surface with no shadow: the dimmed backdrop is what sets it off the page. Title, body and bottom row share one surface with no dividers (as in both design sources), so the panel reads as one plain stack. The title row is 60px with the heading role (heading-4, Inter SemiBold 20). The body has 20px side and 10px vertical padding and scrolls once the panel reaches the viewport; data-type="steps" drops the padding for stacked popup-step sections that carry their own insets. The bottom row is 60px with the actions right-aligned 10px apart; text-button's brackets hang inside each button's 11px padding, so a button is exactly its label plus padding. There is no close (X) control: the design has none, and the bottom row's buttons (plus Escape and a backdrop click) dismiss. Figma's caption slot beside the title and its hidden header action are opacity 0 in every frame and are not modeled.

Sizes: medium 800px (Penpot's panel width; a modal's width is a design decision, not container-driven), small 500px (Figma's confirmation width), large 1173px (Figma's Add project frame, nodes 150:16503 / 150:16475). Backdrop (measured off the design's screens): base/600 gray at 50% behind a centered popup and 30% behind an anchored confirmation. It is a translucent ::before layer, not opacity on the overlay, which would also fade the panel. placement="anchored" sits 10px under its trigger (spacing-3 + spacing-1), never closer than 20px (spacing-6) to a viewport edge, flips above the trigger when it would overflow, and caps its height to the viewport -- measured against documentElement.clientWidth/Height, so a scrollbar gutter doesn't push it past the visible edge.

Body types: "text" (free paragraphs), "input" (Figma's filled textarea, 300px tall in a 320px row), and "gallery" -- a composed gallery filmstrip plus a gallery-image text-icon selector, with a "Reset selection" text-button wired through gallery's generic data-gallery-reset contract, so popup has no gallery-specific code. "gallery" is a deliberately smaller answer to Penpot's "Image-sliders" instance, which nests several sub-widgets that aren't built components.

Behavior (component.js; not sourced -- a design tool doesn't model opening a dialog): a [data-popup-open] trigger shows the matching overlay; any bottom-row button with [data-popup-dismiss] closes it, as do Escape and a backdrop click; both are delegated listeners, so buttons added later work too. Focus moves to the panel on open and back to the trigger on close. Overlays stack: a popup opened from inside another gets a z-index 10 higher (base 100, above dropdown-menu), and Escape and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter act only on the topmost. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter presses the bottom-row action marked data-popup-confirm (template: confirm: true), else a priority=primary one -- every Figma action is a regular-weight secondary button, so primary can't be the only signal. A destructive action (e.g. "Archive selected") uses text-button's error status. Triggers and dismiss buttons are dotted: opening or closing a modal stays in the view. The anchored rule is scoped :not([hidden]) so it never overrides the hidden state. Rendering verified in light and dark themes.
a11y_notes: role="dialog" with aria-labelledby pointing at its title (not in the design source). Implemented: showing and hiding, Escape and backdrop click to close, focus onto the dialog on open and back to the opener on close (also when popups are nested), and Escape / Ctrl+Enter acting only on the topmost popup. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter clicks the confirm button directly, so it is exactly as accessible as clicking it. Not implemented, a real gap: a Tab-cycling focus trap -- Tab can leave an open dialog; a production host should use the native <dialog> element's showModal() or a focus-trap library. The panel keeps a keyboard-only focus ring although Figma draws none. type="gallery" inherits gallery's and gallery-image's own semantics (see their notes).
